clue.text: Weather movement forced cloud up north with reduction in temperature

indicators.note: things that are up in the air are in turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, part of the material to be rearranged
taken as written, part of the material to be rearranged
N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: a word reduced to almost nothing keeps only its opening letter here

parts.note: the word cut down to its first letter, also the standard symbol

explanation.surface: A forecaster describes clouds being pushed northwards as the temperature drops.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two words look like weather talk but are simply letters to shuffle, with N and T added; 'up' is the signal, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the meteorologists' term for the boundary formed when a cold weather system overtakes a warm one.

clue.text: Perhaps this blurred, incomplete picture contributes sporadically to cycle

indicators.note: contributing at scattered points means being slipped in here and there inside another word
something incomplete is missing a piece, here its final letter
a blurred image has its parts smeared out of place, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the word without its final E, then mixed up
taken as written; the jumbled letters are spread through it

explanation.surface: Someone squints at a fuzzy, half-finished image of a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters are not dropped in as one lump but scattered into several gaps, which is what 'sporadically' signals. 'Perhaps this' points at the clue itself, a self-referential definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing being read is itself an example of the puzzle device it names, hence 'perhaps' to flag an example.

clue.text: Subjects like English will expand threshold

indicators.note: to expand is to swell outwards, so a word grows by taking extra letters inside it

parts.note: limen is the technical term for a threshold of perception
e.g. means 'for example', so 'like' in that sense
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A claim that school subjects such as English will open up as a gateway to more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subjects' reads like school subjects but means people under a ruler. The threshold word is a psychology term, and 'like' is the 'for example' abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal vassals owing allegiance to a lord were his subjects, the people bound to serve him.

clue.text: Road one's GP is coming over

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming over another piece means sitting above it, so it goes first

parts.note: a general practitioner is a doctor, abbreviated DR
read as 'one has', i.e. I've, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their family doctor is driving over along a particular road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is a contraction of 'one has', so it becomes I'VE rather than a possessive. A GP is a British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a common name for a street or avenue, as in a residential address.

clue.text: Avoid a failure to trouble the scorers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dodge or evade

definitions.text: a failure to trouble the scorers
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a batsman's score of nought in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone advises sidestepping a sporting flop.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out without scoring has made a duck, so the scorers never had to write anything down.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means dodge; as a cricket noun it is a score of zero runs by a batter.

clue.text: Is avoiding anger over actor becoming politician

parts.note: read as the plural of the letter I: every I is removed

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so these letters are kept out of the words

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger
to do something over is to do it again

explanation.surface: A performer turns to politics while keeping his temper in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is not the verb: it means two I's, and both are dropped, one from IRE and one from AGAIN, leaving RE plus AGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was a Hollywood film star before becoming governor of California and then US president.

clue.text: Clear catch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make as profit after deductions
second meaning: to trap, as with a mesh

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are verbs: to clear a sum is to take it home after costs, and to catch a fish is to land it with a mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning a sum after expenses and trapping something in a mesh are both everyday senses of this verb.

clue.text: Wrongly claimed to possess square in key French market town

indicators.note: possessing something means holding it, so the jumbled word wraps round another
one item placed within another sits inside it
done wrongly means done in the wrong order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed up around the rest
clef is a French word for key
S as a short form of square

explanation.surface: A false claim about who owns the main square of a French market town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' belongs with 'key', not with 'market town': the French word for key, holding the square, sits inside the shuffled letters. The town is in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Macclesfield is a historic Cheshire town in north-west England, long known for its silk trade and weekly markets.

clue.text: A fair few, but no miles at all

indicators.note: 'but no X' means everything except X, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a fair few is a good number
M is the standard abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Someone says there were quite a lot, yet no distance was covered whatsoever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At all' must stand for the answer in sentences like 'is it any better?', meaning 'is it better at all?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb before comparatives, the word means to some degree, the same as 'in the least'.

clue.text: Planter involved with 10cc guitarist

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so these letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the material to be rearranged
the digits read as letters: 1 looks like I, 0 like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener gets mixed up with a guitarist from the 1970s band 10cc.
explanation.walkthrough: 10cc is a real band, which makes it read as a single name; here the digits become the letters I and O and join the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapton is the celebrated English rock and blues player, famed for Cream and 'Layla'.

clue.text: Political neutrality soon upset idle soldiers in Northern Territory

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down entry that turns a word upside down

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
to lig is British slang for lazing about or freeloading

indicators.note: one item placed within another sits inside it

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words, the official abbreviation for this Australian territory
soldiers as the rank and file, men

explanation.surface: Political neutrality is about to be shaken by idle troops in the Australian outback.
explanation.walkthrough: Lig is British slang for lounging about or freeloading at parties; anon is an archaic word for soon. Only the soldiers go inside the territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a state's policy of refusing to join either side of a power bloc, as in the Cold War.

clue.text: React nervously when receiving specific tube

indicators.note: a nervous person fidgets and jitters, so the letters are agitated into a new order
receiving something means taking it in, so another piece goes inside

parts.note: the letters of the word, shuffled
the definite article, which picks out one specific thing

explanation.surface: A patient flinches when a particular medical tube is put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is called the definite article because it refers to a specific item, as against the general 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a thin flexible medical tube inserted into the body to drain or deliver fluids.

clue.text: Arthur's nephew, first in Winchester, taking a cut in profit

indicators.note: something cut in is spliced into the middle of another word

parts.note: a gain is a profit

indicators.note: taking means picking up and joining on, so two pieces are put side by side
the first in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the city name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight from Arthur's family heads to Winchester to take his share of the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester, often linked to Camelot and home to a 'Round Table', supports the Arthurian picture while only supplying a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain, a Knight of the Round Table, is the son of Arthur's sister in most versions of the legend.

clue.text: Mike plugs in 'ABC' to jam timer

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: the run of letters ABC goes from A to C
mike and mic are both short for microphone
to jam is to lock fast, as with gridlock

explanation.surface: Someone plugs a microphone into the ABC broadcaster's studio for a jam session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a name but is a microphone; 'ABC' is read as the span of letters, A to C, written out.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic clock measures time by the vibrations of atoms, making it the world's most precise timekeeper.

clue.text: Local to drink toasts: bottoms up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read from the bottom towards the top
in a down entry the bottom of each word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A pub-goer raises a glass at the local, calling out a cheery drinking toast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition overlaps the wordplay: 'bottoms' and 'up' both do mechanical work and also form the toast itself. A local is a neighbourhood pub in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Scandinavian-style and English drinking cries said just before downing a glass.

clue.text: Special constable in unwanted entrance has look around selection in patisserie

indicators.note: having one thing beside another simply joins them
one item placed within another sits inside it

parts.note: ecce is Latin for 'behold', a look

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: a leak lets something in that should stay out
SC is the abbreviation for a special constable, a volunteer police officer

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman, caught breaking into a bakery, peers round at the pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' becomes the Latin 'ecce' (as in 'ecce homo'). An Eccles cake is a British flaky pastry round filled with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: The currant-filled pastry from Lancashire is one item you might choose from a bakery's display.

clue.text: Chanel business merger?

indicators.note: a merger joins two firms into one, so two pieces are put together

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
the same abbreviation again, the second partner in the deal

explanation.surface: Speculation about the fashion house Chanel being involved in a corporate takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a surname standing for the famous designer's first name; a merger of two companies gives the repeated abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabrielle 'Coco' Chanel, the French couturier, was known by this nickname, so it names her.

clue.text: Mercury coating blade

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the thin metal backing of a mirror, traditionally tin amalgamated with mercury
second meaning: a light fencing sword

explanation.surface: A sword with a coat of silvery metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Old mirrors were backed with a thin sheet of tin and mercury, called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a thin metal sheet used as a reflective backing and the light sword used in fencing.

clue.text: Gap in Features reported from the floor team's sorted

indicators.note: in a down entry, starting from the floor means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to have reported is to have said

indicators.note: something sorted has been rearranged into a different order

parts.note: read as 'team is', with the letters then shuffled

explanation.surface: A heckler from the audience complains that the newspaper's features team is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the floor' suggests an audience member speaking, but in a down entry it means reading upwards. 'Features' here are the face, as in facial features.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists use this term for a space between two teeth, such as the well-known gap between front incisors.

clue.text: Double headed once

indicators.note: headed in the sense of having the head cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: 'of old' means once, in days gone by

explanation.walkthrough: 'Headed' usually means having a head; here it means losing one, like 'topped'.
explanation.definitionFit: To double something over is to bend it back on itself, a common verb sense for creasing paper or cloth.

clue.text: In salute of magician abroad, keeping cool on vacation

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a participle that takes an object

indicators.note: keeping something means holding on to it, so one piece goes inside
abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed up

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle letters

explanation.surface: Tourists applaud a conjuror performing overseas who stays calm while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' looks like a holiday but means the word is vacated, keeping just its first and last letters, which join the scrambled magician.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to praise loudly and publicly, so acclaiming someone means you are saluting them.

clue.text: Nightstick, say, for one getting in with heat

indicators.note: 'X for Y' means X stands in place of Y, one piece swapped for another

parts.note: a nightstick is an example of an arm, a weapon
the Roman numeral for one
the word 'with', which the swap goes into

explanation.surface: A police officer with a truncheon shows up looking for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A nightstick is a police baton; 'say' signals it is one example of an arm, meaning weapon, which replaces the I in 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the quality of being hot, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: On retirement along Riviera, je veux un oiseau local

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
the letters run along consecutive words of the clue without a break

parts.note: the letters sitting across these words

explanation.surface: A retiree on the French Riviera says, in French, 'I want a local bird'.
explanation.walkthrough: The French suits the Riviera setting but is pure decoration; the definition is the French phrase, meaning a local bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Evejar is a regional English dialect name for the nightjar, a bird heard calling at dusk.

clue.text: Top surfaces of sponges intermittently with pepper

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: a surface is the uppermost layer, so each word yields only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words
cum is the Latin word for with

explanation.surface: A recipe step: top the sponge cakes now and then with a sprinkle of pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intermittently' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but it only supplies a first letter; 'with' is Latin cum, as in 'kitchen-cum-dining room'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the genus of sweet and chilli peppers, and the usual name for a bell pepper in many countries.

clue.text: Individual who finds classes challenging not completely hooked

indicators.note: something not complete is short of its end, so the final letter drops

parts.note: a single one, 'a'
a dunce struggles at school, cut short here

explanation.surface: A struggling pupil is only partly gripped by lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The long middle phrase is a roundabout description of a slow learner, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adunc is a rare word from Latin meaning curved inwards like a hook, used of beaks or noses.

clue.text: He makes a hole in one tree

definitions.text: He makes a hole in one
definitions.meaning: first meaning, a whimsical coinage: a golfer who scores an ace

explanation.surface: A golfer gets a hole in one at a tree-lined course.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a hole in one is called an ace, and adding -ER makes a noun for the person who scores one, as baker comes from bake.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus name for maples, often used by gardeners for the ornamental kinds.

clue.text: US actor reportedly understood the attraction of Lord's membership?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the pieces go by their sound

parts.note: to dig is slang for to understand, past tense dug
the Marylebone Cricket Club, which owns Lord's ground
a lure is an attraction

explanation.surface: An American actor grasped why people want to join the club at Lord's cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, owned by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC). Only 'dug' changes spelling to match the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Doug McClure was an American film and TV actor, best known for the western series 'The Virginian'.

clue.text: Regiment once the focus of docudrama

indicators.note: the focus is the centre of attention, so the central letters are taken

parts.note: the three central letters of the nine

explanation.surface: A disbanded army regiment becomes the subject of a television documentary drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' shows the regiment no longer exists: the Ulster Defence Regiment was a British Army unit in Northern Ireland, merged away in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials stand for the Ulster Defence Regiment, a former infantry unit, so it is a former regiment.

clue.text: Hold individual to confess

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate senses of one short word, a verb, an adjective and a second verb.
explanation.definitionFit: It means possess, means belonging to oneself alone, and in older use means admit or acknowledge a fault.

clue.text: Author, high flier, sticks right through reworking of Chaucer

indicators.note: to stick something into a thing is to push it inside
running through something means passing into its interior
reworking material means remaking it in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed up
Rt is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
the skylark is a bird that sings while soaring high

explanation.surface: A writer who is a rising star pushes his way through a modern version of Chaucer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High flier' sounds like praise for the author but is a bird; it and the right abbreviation both go inside the rearranged poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarke was the British science-fiction writer of '2001: A Space Odyssey' and many novels.
